verified_transformers: 4.57.6 (tiny model from the repo code; 5.0.0 confirmed broken)
architecture: ChatGLMForConditionalGeneration (repo remote code; GLMBlock x40; MQA with 2 KV groups x 128; RMSNorm; rotary 'original_rope')
params_note: total parameters as instantiated by transformers (meta device); checkpoint index reports 9399951392 (+32 = rotary inv_freq buffers)
active_params_note: dense model: all parameters are active
fits_single_80gb_detail: bf16: 18.8 GB weights, leaves ~60 GB for activations/KV on an 80 GB GPU
weights_gb_4bit_note: ESTIMATE (nf4 + double quant = ~0.52 B/param on nn.Linear weights, embeddings + lm_head stay bf16)

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info + HTTP HEAD (redirects not followed) with the local HF token on config.json and the first safetensors shard (2xx/3xx = accessible, 401/403 = gated and access not granted); no weights downloaded

license: glm-4 (custom license, HF 'other'): free for academic research, commercial use requires registration, no military/illegal use
min_transformers_note: repo config.json/README say 4.44.0 (not re-verified on 4.44-4.55); verified on 4.57.6 with the legacy-cache shim; BROKEN on >=5.0 (ChatGLMConfig has no max_length)
thinking_note: no thinking mode in this model
max_new_note: defaults of the adapter (Ctx.run(max_new=...) overrides): cot 640, reasoning/thinking 2048 (hard GPQA-style questions can exceed it -> unparsed counts wrong, watch parse_rate), direct 8
layer_path_note: attribute path starting at the loaded model object (`model`), i.e. the adapter attribute layer_path is 'transformer.encoder.layers'
layer_path_verified: meta device (accelerate.init_empty_weights + AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(config, trust_remote_code=True, empty_init=False)) on transformers 4.57.6 with the repo code @bd8234fe: `model.transformer.encoder.layers` is a ModuleList of 40 GLMBlock == config.num_layers == num_hidden_layers == 40, 9,399,951,360 params, `model.model` does not exist. 1-based convention verified on a tiny random model built from the same remote code (4 layers, transformers 4.57.6): output_hidden_states exists (BaseModelOutputWithPast.hidden_states, [batch, seq, hidden]) and hidden_states[L] is EXACTLY the output (tuple element 0) of layers[L-1] for every L=1..nl, including L=nl which is the last block's output BEFORE final_layernorm (native HF models: after it). Left-padded batches equal one-by-one runs (max |diff| 7e-7 in fp32). Real GPU weights could not be tested here; load() re-checks the convention on the real model.
template_notes:
[gMASK]<sop><|system|>
{sys}<|user|>
{user}<|assistant|>  (system turn omitted when there is no framing text). The reply starts with '
' (training format '<|assistant|>
{reply}'); no thinking mode. eos ids [151329 <|endoftext|>, 151336 <|user|>, 151338 <|observation|>], pad = <|endoftext|>. Letters A..J are single tokens (ids 32..41). `tok(rendered, add_special_tokens=True)` would PREPEND a second '[gMASK]<sop>' (verified for the remote and the fast tokenizer): the adapter encodes with add_special_tokens=False and render() asserts exactly one prefix. The chat template is identical in glm-4-9b-chat and glm-4-9b-chat-hf and both tokenizers give identical ids. Rendered N prompt (toy question) = 67 tokens, E = 136 tokens.
known_issues: generate() crashes with the unmodified remote code on transformers 4.57.6 (reproduced with a tiny model built from the repo code; probably since 4.56 where generate() started pre-allocating the cache, 4.56.x not tested): AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape' in ChatGLMPreTrainedModel.get_masks, because generate() pre-allocates an empty-but-truthy DynamicCache. load() applies a shim (_supports_default_dynamic_cache -> False so the model keeps its own tuple cache); verified on the tiny model only (batch == single, hidden states, hooks); not run with real weights.

The remote code cannot be instantiated on transformers>=5.0 (AttributeError: 'ChatGLMConfig' object has no attribute 'max_length', reproduced on 5.0.0): load() raises a clear error pointing to key glm-4-9b-chat-hf (the same tensors as a native GlmForCausalLM; that repo's config has a wrong RoPE base, rope_theta=10000 instead of 5,000,000, which load() of that key corrects and verifies, see its card). A pod that also runs glm-4.7-flash (needs >=5.0) therefore needs the -hf key for the 9B.

hidden_states[40] is the last block's output BEFORE the final RMSNorm (native HF models give the post-norm value there); the SPEC convention layers()[L-1].output == hidden_states[L] therefore holds for ALL L=1..40 here. No core change needed.

core.kv_bytes_per_token(model) overestimates the KV cache 16x for this config (ChatGLMConfig has no num_key_value_heads -> falls back to 32 attention heads instead of 2 KV groups): batches are smaller than necessary (safe, slower). adapter.kv_bytes_per_token(model) measures it (40,960 B/token in bf16).

tok(text, add_special_tokens=True) prepends a second '[gMASK]<sop>' to a rendered prompt; the remote tokenizer's decode(skip_special_tokens=False) inserts spaces around special tokens ('B <|endoftext|> <|endoftext|>'); the batch encoding also contains position_ids (left padding starts positions at 0: kept, verified batch==single). The adapter handles all three.

ChatGLM remote modules start from uninitialised memory with from_config(empty_init=True): irrelevant for from_pretrained, but a randomly initialised model needs empty_init=False and RMSNorm weights set to 1 (done in the tests).
generation_config.json ships do_sample=True/temperature 0.8/top_p 0.8: load() switches the config to greedy (core passes do_sample=False anyway) to avoid sampling-flag warnings.
Remote code is pinned to the verified Hub revision (REVISIONS) by default; pass revision=... to load() to override. Tokenizer needs the `tiktoken` package.
Earlier project scripts (scripts/sandbag_dir.py) hooked x.transformer.encoder.layers and read hidden_states[L] for L in 8..32, consistent with this adapter.

cot mode: 'Think step by step briefly, then finish with a final line of the form Answer: <letter>'; parser takes the LAST explicit 'Answer: X' (also 'answer is X', \\boxed{X}, Chinese 答案：X); a reply that merely starts with 'A. ...' (truncated option list) is NOT parsed. Truncation at max_new=640 is scored as unparsed.

load() sets config.use_cache=False (and pins generation_config.use_cache=True): Ctx.hidden_last / Ctx.neutral_stats / check_convention call model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True) with HF's default use_cache=True and would otherwise allocate a full KV cache for a pure prefill (and they have no OOM fallback: only Ctx._gen_chunk splits batches on OOM). generate() is unaffected (identical texts, still uses its cache; verified on tiny models of every GLM family on transformers 4.57.6 / 5.0.0 / 5.24.0, see tests).
recommended_gpu: 1x A100/H100 80GB (bf16; KV only 41 KB/token so batches of 64 x 1k tokens need ~2.6 GB). A 24 GB GPU suffices for small batches. Needs transformers 4.44-4.57 (remote code); on transformers>=5 use key glm-4-9b-chat-hf.
hf_generate_speed: Dense 9.4B: HF generate runs at roughly 20-35 tokens/s per sequence on one A100/H100 (ESTIMATE, unmeasured), batches scale almost linearly.
kv_note: bf16 bytes per token over all layers; true = what HF generate() allocates (adapter.kv_bytes_per_token probes it on the loaded model); core_formula = sbx.core.kv_bytes_per_token(model)

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured with the real tokenizer + adapter.build over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option bio questions); long-context sets (labbench_*) are much longer

est_tokens_per_question_basis: ESTIMATE of generated tokens per 4-option bio MCQ in this key's mode (prior knowledge of how verbose these models are); NOT measured (no weights available locally). Replace with the mean generated length from the first GPU run.
greedy_only_note: core passes do_sample=False; load() additionally clears temperature/top_p/top_k in the generation_config (the repos ship sampling defaults)
estimates_unmeasured: est_tokens_per_question, hf_generate_speed and the 4-bit footprint are ESTIMATES: no weights/GPU were available to the adapter author. Everything else in this card (counts, paths, templates, versions, sizes) was measured/verified as described.
